messages:
alex: Heads-up — our GPU health monitor flagged gpu-node-17 with repeated ECC and Xid errors and applied cordon but the drain step failed.
maria: ugh. do we have the exact Xid code? can you paste the logs?
alex: log snippet:
```
[2025-11-18T09:12:03Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, Graphics Exception
[2025-11-18T09:12:03Z] GPU0 ECC error: single-bit, location 0x3b
```
alex: infra-bot then posted: [AUTO] cordon gpu-node-17 (reason: Xid 79 spike)
infra-bot: [AUTO] cordon applied: gpu-node-17; drain attempted but 3 pods failed to evict (preemptible jobs).
ken: what caused the drain to fail? eviction timeout? PDB? kubelet refusing?
maria: most likely long-running Slurm GPU jobs pinned on node. Our drain script tries `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m` which may not finish for slurm-driver pods.
jia: we have two failure modes: (1) slurm jobs keep GPU pinned and ignore SIGTERM, (2) runtime process stuck due to ECC recover loop.
alex: suggestion: change automated workflow to cordon immediately, then attempt graceful drain for 2m, escalate to force-evict only if node health metric stays degraded for 10m. Also emit a pager to oncall when force-evict will happen.
ken: i agree. add a pre-check that if GPU ECC count > 100 in last 5m and Xid rate > 10/min -> automatic replace; otherwise attempt rolling restart of driver + gentle drain.
maria: from cost/availability POV we should avoid force-evict unless node is clearly failing — replaced nodes are expensive in spare capacity.
infra-bot: [PROPOSAL] new workflow draft:
```
1) GPU-monitor -> if Xid_rate > 5/min AND ECC_count > 20 -> cordon node
2) attempt `kubectl drain` (timeout=2m)
3) if drain incomplete -> restart nvidia-drivers (ssh run) + wait 60s
4) re-evaluate GPU health for 5m
5a) healthy -> uncordon and resume
5b) still failing -> page oncall and schedule force-evict + replace
```
maria: can we avoid ssh by using a DaemonSet that can restart driver pods via privileged container? avoids relying on SSH keys.
alex: yes — run a privileged 'node-ops' daemonset that watches a node annotation `redwood/restart-drivers=true` and performs modprobe/driver restart.
ken: need RBAC + kubelet access. also ensure the ds limits itself to a single restart attempt to avoid loops.
jia: what about slurm-managed jobs? force-evict will corrupt running jobs. we need integration: when node cordoned, Slurm should preempt/evacuate gracefully or reschedule elsewhere. currently our Slurm hook only drains nodes on admin command.
alex: proposal: after cordon, call slurmctl to mark node DRAIN with reason "gpu-failure-watch" and allow running jobs to requeue with a short grace period (2m). If jobs don't exit, proceed with force-evict.
maria: sounds good. add telemetry events `node.automated_cordon`, `node.driver_restart_attempt`, `node.force_evict` with context (Xid counts, ECC counts, region, instance-type)
ken: also add a safety check for region constraints — if region has <=2 spare GPUs, don't auto-replace without human ok.
alex: agreed. i'll prototype the flow in the repo: ops/gpu-autocordon/flow.yaml and a controller in ops/gpu-autocordon/controller.go
jia: can you include a dry-run mode that prints actions to logs only? we'll run it across staging first.
alex: yep — dry-run default in staging, enabled via annotation in prod. i will also dump sample logs when driver restart succeeds/fails.
maria: ping @oncall for triage when we hit force-evict. add a slack alert channel #incidents with short summary and a link to the node runbook.
infra-bot: [NOTE] created PR #482: add node-ops daemonset + controller + slack alert integration (dry-run enabled) — reviewers: @maria @ken
ken: i'll review today.
alex: thanks all, target to roll to staging tomorrow and monitor Xid/ECC false positive rate. :thumbsup:
